$comment: THE ONLY FILE YOU EDIT TO CHANGE THE POOL.
plugins/agent-pool.ts reads it at config time and rewrites every pooled variant agent
(explore-fast-N, implement-fast-N, context-manager-N) plus the provider whitelists in
opencode.jsonc to match, so the model definitions there are only defaults.
Slot N is the same model for every base agent, which is what makes load shared.
RULES, all validated at startup: models are written provider/model-id, split on the FIRST
slash only so openrouter's vendor-prefixed ids (nvidia/x:free) resolve; must be distinct.
AT MOST 4 SLOTS: opencode.jsonc declares one hidden variant per base per slot, so a
fifth entry would route at an agent that does not exist. Extra entries are dropped
with a warning, not ignored quietly.
WEIGHT is the only knob. Routing is one pass over these slots: lowest ratio wins,
ties go to the lighter slot.
load ratio = (in-flight claims + 2) / weight
so a slot may hold roughly `weight` times the claims of a lighter slot before the pool
prefers the lighter one. The +2 is a free head start for every slot: it is what keeps the
light slots empty as burst headroom instead of spending them on the first claim.
weight 1  fills evenly with its peers; nothing reserved
weight 2  the workhorse: the pool moves on when it holds 2 claims more than a weight-1
slot, which is exactly what the old primary/overflow tiers did
weight 3+ to lean harder on a model you trust more (the per-slot share approaches the
weight ratio once the pool is busy, e.g. 3 vs 1 settles at roughly 3:1)
weight 0.5 to deprioritise a model without removing it from the pool
Absent means weight 1. Must be a number in (0, 100]; anything else warns and uses 1.
Order matters only as a tie-break between slots of equal weight, so the heaviest ones
belong at the top of the list.
WEIGHT IS PER SLOT, not per provider: a slot is compared against every other slot, so
to run one provider's model more often than another's, its weight must beat each
competing slot. Here the opencode-go slot is weight 4 against three weight-1 Zen slots,
which measures 57% opencode-go / 43% Zen. Lower the go weight to 3 for a 50/50 split,
and to 2 for the old 33/67 where the go slot is simply another peer.
Keep the models free (0/0 cost) and tool-call capable. After editing this file run
node tests/refresh-models-snapshot.mjs
which re-checks every slot against models.dev and records the result in
tests/models-snapshot.json. Skipping it fails the pool tests on the new model.
Changing this file requires restarting every opencode process: plugins are not hot-reloaded.
